paper.title: Quantum Algorithm for Online Convex Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization with quantum zeroth-order oracles (general convex losses)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Quantum oracle access: the feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle queried in superposition.
unmapped: feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle Q_f (|x>|q> -> |x>|q+f(x)>) queried O(1) times per round
completely adaptive adversary: f_t chosen after observing x_t
settings.definition_quote: A quantum zeroth-order oracle $Q_f$ is a unitary transformation that maps a quantum state $\ket{x}\ket{q}$ to the state $\ket{x}\ket{q+ f(x)}$ ... the adversary in our setting is \textit{completely adaptive}, who can choose $f_t$ after observing the player's choice $x_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization with classical zeroth-order oracles (O(n) queries per round)
unmapped: completely adaptive adversary: f_t chosen after observing the played point x_t (zeroth-order oracle queried after committing x_t)
settings.definition_quote: A classical zeroth-order oracle $O_f$ to the loss function $f$, queried with a vector $x\in\mathcal{K}$, outputs $O_f(x)=f(x)$. ... The loss functions are G-Lipschitz continuous ... the feasible set $\mathcal{K}$ is bounded and its diameter has an upper bound $D$ ... $\mathcal{K},D,G$ are known to the player.

symbols.rho_q: failure probability of quantum gradient-estimation step per round
symbols.p_q: failure probability of smoothness step per round

conditions: holds with probability greater than 1 - T(rho + p)
tuning: r'_t = rho^2 p / (8 pi sqrt(t n^9)(n+rho))

source.label: TQ
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{QOCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{t}}, r_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{tn}}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{\rho^2 p}{8 \pi \sqrt{tn^9} (n +\rho)}$, can achieve the regret bound $O(DG\sqrt{T})$, with probability greater than $1-T(\rho+p)$, and its query complexity is $O(1)$ in each round.

results.notes: D -> diam_K, G -> L_lip, n -> d. Quantum setting, out of scope. Proof's explicit bound is DG sqrt(T)/2 + 2DG sqrt(T) + DG sqrt(T)/2 + 2G sqrt(T).

conditions: holds with probability greater than 1 - T(rho + p)
tuning: r_t = G^2/(t(2G sqrt(n) + alpha n D))
r'_t = G^2 rho^2 p / (8 pi t n^4 (n+rho)(2G sqrt(n)+alpha n D))

source.label: TAQ
source.quote: For $\alpha$-strongly convex loss functions, Algorithm \ref{QOCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{1}{\alpha t}, r_t=\frac{G^2}{t(2G\sqrt{n}+\alpha nD)}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{G^2\rho^2 p}{8 \pi tn^4 (n +\rho)(2G\sqrt{n}+\alpha nD)}$, can achieve the regret bound $O(G^2\log{T})$, with probability greater than $1-T(\rho+p)$, and its query complexity is $O(1)$ in each round.

results.notes: Proof gives (2G^2/alpha) log T + G^2 log T/2 + G^2 log T; the stated O(G^2 log T) hides the 1/alpha dependence. Recorded as stated.

source.label: TC
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{COCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{t}}, r_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{tn}}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{\delta}{T\sqrt{tn^3}}$ can achieve the regret bound $O(DG\sqrt{T})$, with probability greater than $1-\delta$, and its query complexity is $O(n)$ in each round.

results.notes: Theorem number not printed (likely Theorem 3 per figure). Multi-point feedback with k=2n evaluations per round; failure probability delta passed to algorithm. Bound hides no explicit log(1/delta).
